html:
Coqs is the map's label for western Oregon and southwest Washington in 1500. The name is probably taken from the Coos or the Coquille, peoples of the southern Oregon coast, but the area drawn covers many peoples.

On the coast lived the Coos, Coquille, Tututni and Tillamook; in the Willamette Valley lived the Kalapuya; on the Columbia lived the Chinookan peoples. They fished for salmon, gathered camas roots and acorns, and built plank houses. Europeans did not reach them until the late 1700s. Fur traders came first; disease, the Rogue River Wars of the 1850s and removal to the Siletz and Grand Ronde reservations followed.
